name: Publish Threshold And Creative Iteration
use_when: A project keeps expanding because the editor can always add a better effect, animation, music choice, or story improvement.
The creator wants to improve every video without getting trapped in perfectionism.
The edit needs a final good-enough decision after core QC passes.
avoid_when: The edit has unresolved factual, legal, licensing, safety, or client-required issues.
The current version fails core story, audio, caption, export, or platform QC.
The user explicitly asks for a perfection pass on a high-stakes deliverable.

timeline_pattern.threshold_rule: Publish when the edit meets the defined story, audio, visual, caption, licensing, and export bar, even if more improvements are possible.
timeline_pattern.learning_rule: Try one meaningful new technique per project, document it, and avoid turning the whole project into an endless training loop.
timeline_pattern.hold_rule: Hold only for issues that materially affect viewer understanding, rights, safety, brand, or delivery quality.

motion.rule: Do not add new effects late unless they solve a clear story, focus, or readability problem.

sound.rule: Do not keep searching for better music or SFX after the current choice passes story-fit, license, and mix QC unless it fixes a named weakness.

captions.rule: Caption fixes that affect comprehension outrank decorative caption improvements.

color.rule: Color fixes that preserve detail and consistency outrank late stylistic experiments.

implementation.ffmpeg: Run final probe/decode and contact-sheet checks, then treat nonblocking cosmetic wishes as backlog items.
implementation.remotion: Store publishDecision with blockingIssues, optionalImprovements, learnedTechnique, and nextProjectBacklog.
implementation.blender: Freeze animation changes after core QC unless a render artifact or meaning problem is found.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use a final checklist, export, watch once, fix blockers, and publish rather than endlessly cycling through effects.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Keep an optional improvement marker list separate from blocking QC markers; export when blockers are cleared.

common_mistakes: Treating every possible improvement as a blocker.
Learning too many new techniques inside one project and never publishing.
Publishing with real audio, caption, licensing, export, or story blockers because the editor is tired.
Repeating the same old style forever in the name of efficiency.
qc: Are all blocking story, audio, caption, licensing, export, and readability issues cleared?
Is the remaining improvement list optional rather than blocking?
Was one new technique learned or tested for this project?
Are unfinished experiments moved to a next-project backlog?
Has the creator made an explicit publish or hold decision?
